title: Captivity in the New Testament
body:
15 Minutes w/ The Captains · 2026-01-12

Opens [Rom 15](/bible/romans/15) · [Deut 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28) · [Matt 1](/bible/matthew/1) · [Matt 2](/bible/matthew/2) · [Matt 17](/bible/matthew/17) · [Matt 22](/bible/matthew/22) · [Luke 1](/bible/luke/1) · [Luke 2](/bible/luke/2) · [Luke 24](/bible/luke/24) · [Acts 1](/bible/acts/1) · [John 18](/bible/john/18) · [John 11](/bible/john/11) · [John 19](/bible/john/19) · [John 8](/bible/john/8)
## Introduction *[[0:14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=14s)]* Shalom. Shalom Israel. Captain Osee. I got an officer reading for me, and you are here for another edition of 15 minutes with the captains. Today we got a special topic. Today's topic is titled captivity in the New Testament. That's right. Captivity in the New Testament. A lot of pastors, theologians, for some reason, they think that the captivity that the Israelites went through in the Old Testament is not prevalent in the New. So, we're going to show you that that's not true. ## Scriptures Opened
Reading from an on-screen post by Philip King *[[0:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=48s)]* > I've been studying Israel scattered in the Old Testament versus Israel scattered in the New Testament. - So he's saying he's studying the old versus the new, about the diaspora of our people. > They are not the same. - He says they are not the same. So he's saying that the whole Old Testament does not correlate with the New Testament. That's what these pastors say. > One is attached to the judgment of God against them, and the other is referred to as a spiritual condition. - So from their reading they say no, in the New Testament it is spiritual. It is not physical anymore. There is not a physical captivity taking place when Christ and the disciples were on the earth. Let's see if that's true or not. We're going to get into it and show you out of the Bible that that is not true. It was a physical captivity back then, just as it is a physical captivity today.
**[Romans 15:4](/bible/romans/15#v4)** *[[1:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=97s)]* > [4](/bible/romans/15#v4) For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope. - For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning: so whatever things were written aforetime were written for our learning. So what you must understand, my brother, the captivities are a revolving cycle. They never ended. To this day the children of Israel are under captivity, until Christ cracks the sky and returns. We are still under the curses. The curses were not lifted in the New Testament. Understand that. **[Deuteronomy 28:45-46](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v45)** *[[2:15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=135s)]* > [45](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v45) Moreover all these curses shall come upon thee, and shall pursue thee, and overtake thee, till thou be destroyed; because thou hearkenedst not unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to keep his commandments and his statutes which he commanded thee: > > [46](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v46) And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever. - Moreover all these curses: all these what? All these curses. - Till thou be destroyed: until what? Till thou be destroyed. - And they shall be upon thee for a sign: these curses shall be upon the children of Israel. What? For a sign. - And upon thy seed for ever: hold on. Just for the Old Testament? Just for the Babylonian captivity? And upon thy seed forever. So these curses were going to be upon the children of Israel forever, until what? Christ returned and the curses were done away with. It says there'll be no more curse in Revelation. But that has not happened. So if that has not happened, then the curses are still evident. So let's start in the first book of the New Testament, the book of Matthew, and let's see: when Christ was on the earth, were they free physically, or was it a spiritual condition? **[Matthew 1:16-17](/bible/matthew/1#v16)** *[[3:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=219s)]* > [16](/bible/matthew/1#v16) And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ. > > [17](/bible/matthew/1#v17) So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations; and from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ are fourteen generations. - So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations: from Abraham to David was 14 generations. Also, this is giving you the lineage, letting you know that he has a physical bloodline. - And from David until the carrying away into Babylon: from David unto Babylon. What was taking place? Captivity. The Assyrian captivity. The Babylonian captivity. - And from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ are fourteen generations: and from Babylon you have Babylon, the Persians, the Greeks, and at this present time you have the Romans. So what is it doing? It's letting you know the condition of our people. In the first book, which is what? We were in a state of captivity, as it had been from David all the way up to Christ. That what? There was a savior to come to get us out of the captivity that we're in. But you dumb Christians don't understand that. **[Matthew 2:1](/bible/matthew/2#v1)** *[[4:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=294s)]* > [1](/bible/matthew/2#v1) Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem, - In the days of Herod the king: the days of who? The days of Herod the king. - Behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem: so, let's see. Was this Herod gentleman an Israelite ruling over his people? Because if he was, he would be excited that the king of the Jews that was prophesied about was here to come. Let's see. Was he excited? And let's see what his nationality was. So this is to show you that during the time of Herod, the Israelites at that time knew they were in captivity. They didn't think it was a spiritual condition. They were in a physical captivity.
Reading from *A History of the Jews*, on screen *[[5:43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=343s)]* > Then Herod committed a characteristic blunder. Knowing that the Jews prided themselves upon the fact that their religion tolerated no images, knowing too how cordially the Jews disliked being reminded of their enslavement to Rome, - The Jews disliked what? Being reminded of what? Of their enslavement to Rome. So the Jews knew they were slaves. What the hell are this pastor talking about? They knew they were slaves, and they were slaves to Rome. And when was this? The New Testament. You dumb Christians. > Herod nevertheless placed a huge Roman eagle over the most important gate of the new temple.
Reading from an on-screen page, "Herod the Great, an Edomite, Rules Palestine" *[[6:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=399s)]* > Herod the Great, an Edomite, rules Palestine. Herod the Great was born in the land of Idumea or Edom around 74 BC, which is about when he appears on the Bible timeline chart. He was the son of Antipater of Idumea, who was a high ranking official for Hyrcanus II. - Edom. He was an Edomite, not an Israelite. > Herod was an Edomite that had adopted the customs of the Jews. - Herod was an Edomite. So we had a white man ruling over us in the land of Israel, because Rome gave him dominion to do that. He was a client king to Rome. They said, "Look, you're going to rule over this land, because you grew up as an Israelite. You know their customs, their traditions. You will fit in." Oh, he adopted the customs of the Jews. He was not a Jew. Understand that. Now, let's go back to the Bible for you dumb Negroes.
**[Matthew 2:13](/bible/matthew/2#v13)** *[[8:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=502s)]* > [13](/bible/matthew/2#v13) And when they were departed, behold, the angel of the Lord appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him. - Let's further prove that we were in captivity in the New Testament. - And flee into Egypt: and what? And flee into Egypt. - For Herod will seek the young child to destroy him: ask yourself, why would Herod, being the king of the Jews, be trying to kill his own people, that's supposed to be bringing what? Freedom to his people. Things that make you go hmm. Because what? He was not an Israelite. He was an Idumean, as we just read. **[Matthew 17:24-26](/bible/matthew/17#v24)** *[[9:11](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=551s)]* > [24](/bible/matthew/17#v24) And when they were come to Capernaum, they that received tribute money came to Peter, and said, Doth not your master pay tribute? > > [25](/bible/matthew/17#v25) He saith, Yes. And when he was come into the house, Jesus prevented him, saying, What thinkest thou, Simon? of whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute? of their own children, or of strangers? > > [26](/bible/matthew/17#v26) Peter saith unto him, Of strangers. Jesus saith unto him, Then are the children free. - Let's get further proof that they were in captivity. - Of whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute? of their own children, or of strangers: do you take custom or tribute of your own people or strangers? - Peter saith unto him, Of strangers: Peter said we take custom of strangers when you in rulership. - Then are the children free: hold on. He said then are the children free. Christ told Peter, okay, well, when you are able to have tax and tribute, that's when we free as a people. Peter, we not free right now, Peter. We in slavery, Peter, because Rome is ruling over us, Peter. But you dumb Christians don't read the Bible. The same way it was then is the same way it is now. Y'all think y'all free. You're not free. **[Matthew 22:17-21](/bible/matthew/22#v17)** *[[10:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=617s)]* > [17](/bible/matthew/22#v17) Tell us therefore, What thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give tribute unto Cesar, or not? > > [18](/bible/matthew/22#v18) But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said, Why tempt ye me, ye hypocrites? > > [19](/bible/matthew/22#v19) Shew me the tribute money. And they brought unto him a penny. > > [20](/bible/matthew/22#v20) And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription? > > [21](/bible/matthew/22#v21) They say unto him, Cesar’s. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Cesar the things which are Cesar’s; and unto God the things that are God’s. - Is it lawful to give tribute unto Cesar, or not: is it lawful to give taxes unto Caesar? They was trying to catch him up. - Shew me the tribute money: hold on. Do what? Show me the tribute money. - Render therefore unto Cesar the things which are Cesar's; and unto God the things that are God's: so he said, look at this money. Is that our image on the money? No. What is he showing you? Captivity. Slaves.
Reading from an on-screen description of the Roman denarius *[[11:08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=668s)]* > The Roman denarius, a silver coin, was widely used by Jewish people in the first century AD, including for paying taxes to the Roman emperors. - Well, dog on it. I thought it was spiritual. Why are they using physical money to pay Roman emperors if they were in rulership? I thought it was a spiritual captivity. Huh? > The denarius was a standard unit of currency in Roman society and was also used for daily transactions. > Use: the denarius was used for paying the Roman tribute, a tax imposed by the Roman emperors on the Jewish people. - Oh, that's why, because they were under taxes. They were in captivity.
**[Luke 1:68-74](/bible/luke/1#v68)** *[[12:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=725s)]* > [68](/bible/luke/1#v68) Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, > > [69](/bible/luke/1#v69) And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David; > > [70](/bible/luke/1#v70) As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: > > [71](/bible/luke/1#v71) That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us; > > [72](/bible/luke/1#v72) To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant; > > [73](/bible/luke/1#v73) The oath which he sware to our father Abraham, > > [74](/bible/luke/1#v74) That he would grant unto us, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear, - These are not hard sayings that we're reading here. But because our people do not read the Bible with their eyes open, because we think we all one people, you don't understand it. You don't get it. Just like you black people today think you free here in America. You're not free. This is not your land. You were brought here as slaves. - That we should be saved from our enemies: who was he speaking about? The other nations. Why would they need to be saved? Why would he understand that? Because they knew when Christ came, to be freed from what? Roman rule. - That we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies: that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies, because at that time the Romans were ruling over them. - Might serve him without fear: what was the fear that they were worried about? That all their children two years and under would be murdered, that they have to pay taxes, that they would have to sacrifice unto other gods like they did during the Grecian captivity and others. But y'all don't understand the Bible. **[Luke 2:1](/bible/luke/2#v1)** *[[13:43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=823s)]* > [1](/bible/luke/2#v1) And it came to pass in those days, that there went out a decree from Cesar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed. - That all the world should be taxed: talking about what? The Israelite world, wherever the Jews were at, whoever was under Roman dominion, the Roman Empire. Taxes went out. That's what happened. And guess who fell under that? Israel. Because when you read the next verses down, Joseph and Mary went up to pay their taxes. Interesting. **[Luke 24:20-21](/bible/luke/24#v20)** *[[14:18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=858s)]* > [20](/bible/luke/24#v20) And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him. > > [21](/bible/luke/24#v21) But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel: and beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done. - So what are we showing you? Showing you that in the New Testament we were in a state of slavery. - But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel: hold on. Which what? Which should have redeemed Israel. Why would they need him to redeem Israel? They weren't talking about a future. They were talking about right then. They thought Christ was bringing the kingdom then. Dominion then. Why would they need dominion? Why would they need rulership? Because they were slaves. **[Acts 1:6](/bible/acts/1#v6)** *[[15:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=907s)]* > [6](/bible/acts/1#v6) When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel? - Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel: what he was asking? When are you going to restore us to a level of rulership and dominion? They weren't asking about no spiritual rulership. A physical position on the earth. That is what they were asking for, because they were in physical servitude and slavery. But y'all don't understand. Y'all can't get it. **[John 18:31](/bible/john/18#v31)** *[[15:41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=941s)]* > [31](/bible/john/18#v31) Then said Pilate unto them, Take ye him, and judge him according to your law. The Jews therefore said unto him, It is not lawful for us to put any man to death: - Further proof that they were slaves. - Take ye him, and judge him according to your law: Pilate said, "Hey, if y'all want to kill him, take him and judge him according to your law." Because he knew what they was doing was wicked when they was setting up Christ. - It is not lawful for us to put any man to death: why was it not lawful for them to put any man to death? Because they were not the ruling class. They had no power. Rome had to sign off on any and everything they did. Understand that. **[John 11:47-48](/bible/john/11#v47)** *[[16:25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=985s)]* > [47](/bible/john/11#v47) Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. > > [48](/bible/john/11#v48) If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation. - For this man doeth many miracles: this man doeth many miracles. - And the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation: then the Romans, the physical people of the Romans, will do what? They will come and take away both our place and nation. Hold on. The Romans were going to come and take away their place and nation if they didn't handle Christ the way they needed to. Showing what? They had to answer to somebody else, and they were worried about that. **[John 19:15](/bible/john/19#v15)** *[[17:11](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=1031s)]* > [15](/bible/john/19#v15) But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cesar. - Shall I crucify your King: shall I crucify your king? He was being funny. - The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cesar: they said, "We have no king but Caesar." Why were the Jews saying that their king was Caesar, who was a Roman? Because they were in slavery. Just like today, ask a negro who his king is. He going to say President Trump or Joe Biden or JFK. Same thing today. **[John 8:32-33](/bible/john/8#v32)** *[[17:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=1074s)]* > [32](/bible/john/8#v32) And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free. > > [33](/bible/john/8#v33) They answered him, We be Abraham’s seed, and were never in bondage to any man: how sayest thou, Ye shall be made free? - This is the same spirit that's on the earth today. Our people don't accept that we are in slavery, that we are in captivity. But it's evident as you read throughout the scriptures. Back then, it's the same today. - And the truth shall make you free: Christ said, "Hey, the truth is going to make you free, cuz right now we slaves." - We be Abraham's seed, and were never in bondage to any man: they thought they weren't in bondage, just like the Negro I posted at the start of this video. He said they weren't in slavery. It's a spiritual thing. No, Christ showed you different. The disciples showed you different. - How sayest thou, Ye shall be made free: how you going to say we going to be free? We ain't never been enslaved. A lot of y'all got that same thought and mindset today. ## In Closing *[[18:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0&t=1125s)]* So hopefully you got something out of that. That's 15 minutes with the captains, captivity in the New Testament. With that, we say shalom. --- [15 Minutes Index](/captains) · [Watch the full session on YouTube ↗](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_g8W7w0yr0)
